knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Grid squares have side length one unit.

![](images/75/754ad5c58e27842a9f7896890394a58401f7f3066f65183374ad3c1cdca585b2.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\mathbf{b}$ from $O$, ending at $B$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OB} &=1\,(0, 4)=(0, 4). \\
\overrightarrow{BC} &=(6, 0).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/f4/f4be6a4a52dc9bba50ec3d872ef3617166f0bce01cb28397ef3416bef114f77a.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{a}$, whose grid displacement is $(2, 0)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{6}{2}=3
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{a}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{BC}=3\mathbf{a}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OB}+\overrightarrow{BC} \\
&=\mathbf{b}+3\mathbf{a} \\
&=3\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{a}$ gives $\lambda=3$.
